lecture_Day12.MO_rule_p7: Take all the valence atomic orbitals of the atoms and redistribute them over the whole molecule; one molecular orbital comes out for every atomic orbital put in.
lecture_Day12.HOMO_LUMO_p11: HOMO = highest occupied molecular orbital; LUMO = lowest unoccupied molecular orbital.
lecture_Day12.Na2_Na4_p19_21: Na2: one filled MO below the 3s level and one empty MO above it (the HOMO-LUMO gap). Na4: four MOs from 3s, two filled, two empty; 'As we add more and more atoms (and electrons) to the MO diagram, the HOMO-LUMO gap gets smaller quickly.'
lecture_Day12.NaN_ZnN_p22_23: Na_N: the 3s MOs form a band, lower half occupied, upper half empty (partially filled valence band), overlapping the empty 3p band. Zn_N: the 4s band is filled (valence band) and overlaps the empty 4p band (conduction band).
lecture_Day12.conductor_rule_p18: Any material with a partially filled valence band or a filled valence band that overlaps with an empty conduction band is an electrical conductor. Any material with a large enough band gap acts as an insulator. And then there are the metalloids...
lecture_Day12.band_sketch_p24: Insulator (diamond): filled band, large gap, empty band. Conductor (zinc): filled band touching an empty band. Conductor (sodium): band filled only in its lower part. Semiconductor (silicon): filled band, small gap, empty band. 'T up' (silicon heated): a strip of electrons at the bottom of the upper band and empty strip at the top of the lower band; same gap.
lecture_Day12.doping_p25: Pure Si: valence band, gap Eg, conduction band; Lewis symbol of Si with 4 dots. n-type: 'Phosphorus donor level' just below the conduction band; P has 5 dots. p-type: 'Gallium acceptor level' just above the valence band, with + marks (holes) at the top of the valence band; Ga has 3 dots.
lecture_Day12.metals_p17: Metals: malleable, ductile, lustrous, heat and electricity conductors, relatively large densities, high melting points, solids except Hg, tend to form cations.

textbook_preview_18_5_PDF920.P_donor_level: about 4 kJ/mol below the Si conduction band
textbook_preview_18_5_PDF920.Ga_acceptor_level: about 7 kJ/mol above the Si valence band
textbook_preview_18_5_PDF920.holes: valence electrons that move into the acceptor level leave positively charged holes; electrons migrating between holes carry current (p-type)
